title_en: GOP state officials push to revive Trump's mail voting restrictions for 2028 election
title_zh: 共和党州官员推动恢复特朗普对 2028 年大选的邮件投票限制
summary: Some Republican state officials are reviving a bid for mail-in voting restrictions for the 2028 election by appealing a court order blocking the Postal Service from carrying out a revised ballot rule.
summary_zh: 一些共和党州官员正在对法院阻止 Posta 的命令提出上诉，以重启对 2028 年大选邮寄投票的限制。
body_en: GOP state officials appeal block on 2028 mail voting limits : NPR

GOP state officials appeal block on 2028 mail voting limits Some Republican state officials are reviving a bid for mail-in voting restrictions for the 2028 election by appealing a court order blocking the Postal Service from carrying out a revised ballot rule.
An election worker sorts mail-in ballots at the Miami-Dade County Supervisor of Elections Office in Doral for Florida's primary election in August. Lynne Sladky/AP hide caption
Voting for this year's midterm elections just concluded, but Republican officials in a number of states are already looking to shape how votes are cast in 2028.
Twelve GOP state attorneys general are pushing to revive the president's bid for mail-in voting restrictions in time for the 2028 election.

On Thursday, they started the process of appealing a September order by U.S. District Judge Carl Nichols, one of the two judges who blocked the U.S. Postal Service from carrying out a plan released in response to an executive order by President Trump .

The Republican state attorneys general represent Alabama, Florida, Indiana, Kansas, Louisiana, Missouri, Montana, Nebraska, Oklahoma, South Carolina, South Dakota and Texas. It's not clear, however, how long some of these states will continue this case, given that Democrats won up and down the ballot in the midterms. In Texas and Kansas, Democratic candidates are set to take control of their states' attorney general's offices in January.
The Trump administration's voter roll crusade could continue

In September, the Supreme Court refused to pause a similar ruling by U.S. District Judge Indira Talwani, who is based in Boston. That order stopped USPS from working on its revised rule for federal ballot mail, but it only applied to this year's midterm elections.
Nichols' preliminary injunction blocks USPS from implementing the plan for all federal elections, including the 2028 race.

It's not clear if the Trump administration plans to appeal Nichols' ruling by Friday's deadline for filing a court notice. Asked about the Justice Department's plans, DOJ spokesperson Matthew Tragesser replied in an email that the department doesn't comment on ongoing litigation.
The blocked rule — which the Postal Service released in late August — would require states to turn over lists of voters' names and addresses in order to have them delivered by USPS.
Tens of millions cast ballots for midterms despite worries of Trump's interference
Nichols, a Washington, D.C.-based judge who was nominated by Trump, found that the mailing agency likely has no power to impose that requirement on states.

"As the Government concedes, the Postal Service could issue (and enforce) the Rule only if Congress gave it the authority to do so, but here no statute grants the Postal Service the power to issue key parts of the Rule," Nichols wrote.

The administration's earlier push to put these new restrictions in place for the midterms alarmed many election officials, who were concerned about last-minute changes causing major disruptions to the tens of millions who regularly vote by mail. Some voters with disabilities and those in places without polling sites, they feared, could have lost the ability to exercise their right to cast a ballot.
While the Supreme Court ultimately stopped implementation of the USPS rule for the midterms, Justices Samuel Alito and Clarence Thomas dissented from that ruling.

Fellow conservative Justice Brett Kavanaugh said in a concurring opinion that he believed state and local election officials did not have enough time to "reasonably implement the rule" this time. But Kavanaugh noted that "there is at least a fair prospect that the final rule falls within the Postal Service's statutory authority."

body_zh: 共和党州官员对 2028 年邮件投票限制的阻止提出上诉：NPR
共和党州官员对阻止 2028 年邮寄投票限制提出上诉一些共和党州官员正在对法院阻止邮政局执行修订后的投票规则的命令提出上诉，以重启对 2028 年选举邮寄投票限制的提议。
一名选举工作人员在位于多拉尔的迈阿密戴德县选举办公室主管处对佛罗里达州 8 月份初选的邮寄选票进行分类。琳恩·斯拉基/美联社隐藏标题栏
今年中期选举的投票刚刚结束，但一些州的共和党官员已经在考虑制定 2028 年的投票方式。
十二名共和党州总检察长正在推动总统在 2028 年大选前及时恢复邮寄投票限制的提议。
周四，他们开始对美国地区法官卡尔·尼科尔斯 (Carl Nichols) 9 月份的命令提出上诉，卡尔·尼科尔斯是阻止美国邮政局执行针对特朗普总统行政命令而发布的计划的两名法官之一。
共和党州检察长代表阿拉巴马州、佛罗里达州、印第安纳州、堪萨斯州、路易斯安那州、密苏里州、蒙大拿州、内布拉斯加州、俄克拉荷马州、南卡罗来纳州、南达科他州和德克萨斯州。然而，鉴于民主党在中期选举中获胜，目前尚不清楚其中一些州将继续这种情况多久。在德克萨斯州和堪萨斯州，民主党候选人将于一月份控制该州的总检察长办公室。
特朗普政府的选民名册运动可能会继续
9月，最高法院拒绝暂停美国波士顿地区法官英迪拉·塔尔瓦尼(Indira Talwani)的类似裁决。该命令阻止美国邮政局制定联邦选票邮件的修订规则，但仅适用于今年的中期选举。
尼科尔斯的初步禁令阻止 USPS 实施所有联邦选举的计划，包括 2028 年的竞选。
目前尚不清楚特朗普政府是否计划在周五提交法庭通知的最后期限前对尼科尔斯的裁决提出上诉。当被问及司法部的计划时，司法部发言人马修·特拉杰瑟在一封电子邮件中回复说，司法部不会对正在进行的诉讼发表评论。
邮政服务于八月下旬发布的封锁规则将要求各州交出选民姓名和地址清单，以便由美国邮政局投递。
尽管担心特朗普的干涉，仍有数千万人为中期选举投票
由特朗普提名的华盛顿特区法官尼科尔斯发现，邮政机构可能无权将这一要求强加于各州。
尼科尔斯写道：“正如政府承认的那样，只有国会授权邮政服务才能发布（并执行）该规则，但没有任何法规授予邮政服务发布该规则关键部分的权力。”
政府早些时候推动在中期选举中实施这些新的限制措施，令许多选举官员感到震惊，他们担心最后一刻的变化会对数千万定期通过邮寄投票的人造成重大干扰。他们担心，一些残疾选民和那些没有投票站的地方的选民可能会失去行使投票权的能力。
虽然最高法院最终停止执行美国邮政局关于中期选举的规则，但法官塞缪尔·阿利托和克拉伦斯·托马斯对该裁决持有异议。
同为保守派的法官布雷特·卡瓦诺在一份一致意见中表示，他认为州和地方选举官员这次没有足够的时间“合理地执行该规则”。但卡瓦诺指出，“最终规则至少有可能属于邮政服务的法定权力范围。”

title_en: Trump-backed Maga firebrand Lauren Boebert defeated in Colorado congressional race
title_zh: 特朗普支持的马加煽动者劳伦·博伯特在科罗拉多州国会竞选中击败
summary: US congresswoman, who has been caught up in repeated controversies, loses re-election bid to Democrat Eileen Laubacher Lauren Boebert, the firebrand conservative Republican Colorado representative whose three terms in Congress have been marred by multiple cont
summary_zh: 屡屡陷入争议的美国女众议员连任，输给了民主党人、煽动者艾琳·劳巴赫·劳伦·博伯特 (Eileen Laubacher Lauren Boebert)。
body_en: Trump-backed Maga firebrand Lauren Boebert defeated in Colorado congressional race | US midterm elections 2026
US congresswoman, who has been caught up in repeated controversies, loses re-election bid to Democrat Eileen Laubacher
Lauren Boebert, the firebrand conservative Republican Colorado representative whose three terms in Congress have been marred by multiple controversies, was defeated in her re-election bid.
The gun rights advocate, born-again Christian and one-time QAnon fan lost to Democrat Eileen Laubacher by a less than 1% margin, according to the Associated Press.

“I’m honored by the trust the people of Colorado’s fourth district have placed in me. This campaign was never about party labels. It was about putting people first,” Laubacher said in a statement. “To those who voted for me, thank you, I will strive to make you proud. To those who didn’t, I’ll fight just as hard for you and hope to earn your support.”

This district, which spans the eastern plains of Colorado, is one of the state’s most conservative seats and has long been a Republican stronghold. Laubacher is a retired two-star navy rear admiral, who was deployed to Afghanistan and later worked on the national security council under the Biden administration.

Laubacher just became a registered Democrat in 2025, saying in a debate with Boebert the Republican party had become “nearly unrecognizable”. She focused her campaign on decades of military and national security service.
In a statement congratulating Laubacher, Suzan DelBene, chair of the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee, declared: “Lauren Boebert’s sideshow is over.”

Both Laubacher and Boebert moved to Colorado’s fourth congressional district in recent years. Boebert accused Laubacher of moving there and changing parties in order to run for Congress. Likewise, Boebert has been questioned for her move to the district in 2024 after barely eking out a win in the third district’s previous election.

Boebert said the move was because of “dark money” flowing from Hollywood to “steal” district three’s congressional seat: “It’s coming from Hollywood … when you have Barbra Streisand coming in and donating to the Democrat, when you have Ryan Reynolds coming in and donating to the Democrat … It shows you that Hollywood is trying to buy their way into Congress.”

Boebert’s tenure in Congress has been racked with controversy. She decried the 2020 presidential election as being rigged, demanded to carry a handgun on the House floor and was accused of helping incite the January 6 insurrection by tweeting “Today is 1776” the morning of the riots, among other actions. Boebert later condemned the attack on the Capitol.

She went viral in 2023 when she was filmed groping her date, vaping and being escorted out of a Beetlejuice musical in Denver in 2023. Initially, Boebert joked that she would “plead guilty to laughing and singing too loud”, but the incident later led to her publicly apologizing and divorcing her husband (who was not her date).

And just weeks before the election, she was hit by an ethics complaint over allegations she had sexual relationships with three staffers and had paid one to stay silent, allegations she has denied and called “politically motivated”.

Despite the dust-ups and being a Maga loyalist, Boebert did occasionally stand up to Trump. She was one of the most vocal members of Congress calling for the release of the Epstein files, even after the White House tried to persuade her to remove her name from a discharge petition for the documents.

This earned the ire of Trump, who has called Boebert a “carpetbagger” and “dumb”. The president’s first veto of his second term was for a bill sponsored by Boebert that would have funded a drinking water project in district four. The bill had passed the House and Senate unanimously.

“Nothing says ‘America First’ like denying clean drinking water to 50,000 people in south-east Colorado many of whom enthusiastically voted for him all three elections,” Boebert said in a statement at the time.
“But hey, if this administration wants to make its legacy blocking projects that deliver water to rural Americans; that’s on them.”
body_zh: 特朗普支持的马加煽动者劳伦·博伯特在科罗拉多州国会竞选中击败| US midterm elections 2026
屡遭争议的美国女众议员连任惨败给民主党人艾琳·劳巴赫 (Eileen Laubacher)
劳伦·博伯特(Lauren Boebert)是科罗拉多州一位煽动性的保守派共和党众议员，她在国会的三个任期都因多重争议而受到损害，她在连任竞选中落败。
据美联社报道，这位枪支权利倡导者、重生的基督徒和曾经的 QAnon 粉丝以不到 1% 的优势输给了民主党人艾琳·劳巴赫 (Eileen Laubacher)。
劳巴赫在一份声明中表示：“科罗拉多州第四选区人民对我的信任让我感到很荣幸。这次竞选活动从来都不是为了政党标签。而是为了以人为本。” “对于那些投票给我的人，谢谢你们，我会努力让你们感到骄傲。对于那些没有投票的人，我会同样努力为你们而战，并希望赢得你们的支持。”
该选区横跨科罗拉多州东部平原，是该州最保守的席位之一，长期以来一直是共和党的大本营。劳巴赫是一名退役两星海军少将，曾被部署到阿富汗，后来在拜登政府领导下的国家安全委员会工作。
劳巴赫于 2025 年刚刚成为注册民主党人，他在与博伯特的辩论中表示，共和党已经变得“几乎认不出来了”。她的竞选重点是数十年的军事和国家安全服务。
民主党国会竞选委员会主席苏珊·德尔贝尼在一份祝贺劳巴赫的声明中宣称：“劳伦·博伯特的余兴节目结束了。”
近年来，劳巴赫和博伯特都搬到了科罗拉多州第四国会选区。博伯特指责劳巴赫搬到那里并更换政党以竞选国会议员。同样，博伯特在上一次第三选区选举中勉强获胜后，于 2024 年搬到该选区也受到质疑。
博伯特表示，此举是因为“黑钱”从好莱坞流向“窃取”第三区的国会席位：“它来自好莱坞……当芭芭拉·史翠珊进来并向民主党捐款时，当瑞恩·雷诺兹进来并向民主党捐款时……这表明好莱坞正在试图收买进入国会。”
博伯特在国会的任期一直饱受争议。她谴责 2020 年总统选举被操纵，要求在众议院携带手枪，并被指控在骚乱当天早上发布推文“今天是 1776 年”，从而帮助煽动 1 月 6 日的叛乱等。博伯特后来谴责了对国会大厦的袭击。
2023 年，她被拍到在丹佛摸索约会对象、吸电子烟并被护送离开丹佛的 Beetlejuice 音乐剧，这让她走红。最初，博伯特开玩笑说她会“承认笑声和歌声太大”，但这一事件后来导致她公开道歉并与丈夫（不是她的约会对象）离婚。
就在选举前几周，她遭到道德投诉，指控她与三名员工发生性关系，并付钱让一名员工保持沉默，但她否认了这些指控，并称其“出于政治动机”。
尽管存在风波，而且作为马加的忠实拥护者，博伯特偶尔也会反抗特朗普。她是要求公布爱泼斯坦文件最强烈的国会议员之一，即使白宫试图说服她从这些文件的释放请愿书中删除她的名字。
这引起了特朗普的愤怒，他称博伯特是“地毯式的骗子”和“愚蠢的人”。总统第二任期的第一次否决是针对由博伯特发起的一项法案，该法案将为第四区的饮用水项目提供资金。该法案已在众议院和参议院一致通过。
博伯特在当时的一份声明中表示：“没有什么比拒绝向科罗拉多州东南部 5 万人提供清洁饮用水更能体现‘美国优先’了，其中许多人在三场选举中都热情地投票给了他。”
“但是，嘿，如果本届政府想要继续实施其遗留的封锁项目，为美国农村地区供水；那就由他们来做吧。”

summary_zh: 特朗普官员寻求推翻下级法院的裁决，该裁决认为禁止庇护申请的行政命令非法 美国最高法院周五同意
body_en: US supreme court agrees to consider Trump’s ban on asylum at US-Mexico border | US supreme court
Trump officials seek to overturn lower court rulings that found executive order banning asylum applications illegal
The US supreme court agreed on Friday to consider Donald Trump’s ban on asylum at the US-Mexico border , a pillar of the Republican president’s far-reaching crackdown on immigration.
The Trump administration wants to overturn lower court decisions that found the executive order banning asylum applications is illegal.
Federal law gives people the right to seek asylum if they fear persecution in their home countries, no matter how they arrived in the US.

At the same time, it also allows the executive branch to decide whether people are granted asylum. The Trump administration argues it can categorically deny asylum to migrants covered by the order and should not have to accept applications destined to be rejected.
Federal attorneys say years-long processing times had previously contributed to an influx of migrants at the southern border as many were released into the country while awaiting a decision.
But immigration attorneys at the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) and National Immigrant Justice Center counter that border crossings were already falling before Trump took office.
They say his executive order is an attempt to unilaterally “eviscerate” legal protections aimed at protecting people fleeing danger in their home countries.

The executive branch does decide whether to grant asylum, which allows people to live and work legally in the US. But those decisions are supposed to be made on an individual basis and the law doesn’t allow the president to unilaterally stop people from even applying, those attorneys argue.
The asylum ban was one of a series of immigration restrictions Trump rolled out upon his return to office in 2025. It has remained in place during the litigation.
body_zh: 美国最高法院同意考虑特朗普在美墨边境的庇护禁令美国最高法院
特朗普官员寻求推翻下级法院的裁决，该裁决认为禁止庇护申请的行政命令非法
美国最高法院周五同意考虑唐纳德·特朗普在美墨边境的庇护禁令，这是这位共和党总统影响深远的移民镇压的一个支柱。
特朗普政府希望推翻下级法院裁定禁止庇护申请的行政命令非法的裁决。
联邦法律规定，如果人们担心在本国受到迫害，无论他们如何到达美国，他们都有权寻求庇护。
同时，它还允许行政部门决定是否给予人们庇护。特朗普政府辩称，它可以断然拒绝向该命令所涵盖的移民提供庇护，并且不必接受注定会被拒绝的申请。
联邦检察官表示，长达数年的处理时间导致了南部边境大量移民涌入，因为许多人在等待决定期间被释放到该国。
但美国公民自由联盟（ACLU）和美国国家移民司法中心的移民律师反驳说，在特朗普就职之前，过境人数就已经在下降。
他们表示，他的行政命令试图单方面“废除”旨在保护逃离祖国危险的人们的法律保护。
行政部门确实决定是否给予庇护，这允许人们在美国合法生活和工作。但这些律师认为，这些决定应该根据个人情况做出，法律不允许总统单方面阻止人们提出申请。
庇护禁令是特朗普在 2025 年重返办公室后推出的一系列移民限制措施之一。该禁令在诉讼期间一直有效。

title_en: ICE reports record immigration arrests, deportations since Trump White House return
title_zh: 自特朗普重返白宫以来，ICE 报告记录了移民逮捕和驱逐出境的情况
summary: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement says it arrested and deported more people during a recent 12-month period than at any time in its 23-year history

body_en: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement says it arrested and deported more people during a recent 12-month period than at any time in its 23-year history
WASHINGTON -- U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement said Thursday that it arrested and deported more people during a recent 12-month period than at any time in its 23-year history.

ICE said it deported 483,200 people in the fiscal year that ended Sept. 30, up 9% from its previous high of 442,640 in the same period a year earlier and up 78% from 271,480 in 2024, the last year of Joe Biden's presidency.
ICE arrested 474,850 people in the most recent 12-month period, roughly double the 239,890 arrests a year earlier and more than quadruple the 113,430 arrests in 2024.
ICE had not released such precise counts since President Donald Trump returned to the White House, including for 2025.

华盛顿——美国移民和海关执法局周四表示，在最近 12 个月内逮捕和驱逐的人数比其 23 年历史上的任何时候都要多。
ICE表示，在截至9月30日的财年中，驱逐了483,200人，比去年同期的442,640人的最高纪录增加了9%，比2024年（乔·拜登总统任期的最后一年）的271,480人增加了78%。
ICE 在最近 12 个月内逮捕了 474,850 人，大约是一年前逮捕人数 239,890 人的两倍，是 2024 年逮捕人数 113,430 人的四倍多。

body_en: FRIENDS WITH (SNAP) BENEFITS: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani unveiled the latest perk of his chummy relationship with President Donald Trump, announcing a deal today that will give stores across the country more time to comply with changes to federal food assistance rules.
New rules from the Department of Agriculture, which took effect last week, required retailers to stock a greater diversity of products in order to continue receiving SNAP benefits.

Just before they kicked in, Mamdani signed onto a bipartisan letter to USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins urging the Trump administration to delay implementing the new requirements. He warned the rules would threaten the viability of the city’s more than 10,000 bodegas and corner stores, as well as the New Yorkers who rely on them, if the stores could not meet the mandates in time and lost the ability to accept SNAP payments.

Now, after negotiations with Rollins and foe-turned-bro Trump, Mamdani secured a 90-day extension for small retailers to comply with the rules — not just in New York City, but nationwide. The extension starts Friday.
Mamdani said he personally escalated the extension request to President Trump after City Hall reached out to the federal government.

“What I told the president was that this is a rule that, if allowed to be implemented on the timeline as it was scheduled, would be one that would throw the lives of so many working New Yorkers into a real place of anxiety and chaos,” he said. “And the president took that concern seriously.”
Mamdani declined to share how often he chats with Trump — “I’ll keep the cadence of that between the two of us,” he said — but he emphasized their conversations are ongoing.
As the two executives approach the one-year anniversary of their unexpected bromance, today’s announcement serves as a reminder that Mamdani’s Trump strategy has largely paid off.

After a seemingly love-struck Trump emerged from the duo’s first Oval Office meeting on Nov. 21, the threat of an immigration enforcement surge on par with Minneapolis largely evaporated, eliminating a potentially explosive situation that at the time loomed over the mayor’s early days in office.

In February, Mamdani successfully petitioned Trump to release a Columbia University student who had been taken into the custody by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement and, as POLITICO reported this week , Mamdani has continued to make those requests privately to the president. The two have also discussed the federal government’s involvement in a massive development project that would span the Sunnyside Yard rail depot in Queens.
The price for these spoils has so far been one Mamdani’s base is willing to accept.

The mayor rarely, if ever, criticizes Trump directly. He demurs when asked by reporters about their private phone calls. And during a joint appearance outside Gracie Mansion in late September, when asked about Trump’s short-lived White House media ban, Mamdani only said that he himself supported having a variety of news outlets covering City Hall. — Molly Reinmann and Joe Anuta
NVIDIA AND BEYOND: Gov. Kathy Hochul isn’t worried that the scandal engulfing former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang will impact the broader semiconductor sector.

“It’s a resilient industry,” she said today. “We’ve already planted the flag in places from Malta and all the way to Syracuse. New York’s economy will continue to be sound and continue to grow. This will not have an effect on meeting our obligations to continue the investments and create more jobs.”

New York has placed a massive, long-term bet on the industry, which has toeholds in the Syracuse area and the Saratoga County town of Malta, where Hochul appeared today to tout the groundbreaking of a new chip manufacturing facility.
Huang resigned amid allegations of multiple affairs, including a relationship with a woman who may be a potential Chinese spy .
The tech boom has helped lift Wall Street and swell New York’s coffers. A slowdown may spell trouble for the economy. — Nick Reisman
LEADERSHIP MOVES: State Sen. Liz Krueger told Playbook today she isn’t angling to chair the body’s housing committee.
“I’m not going to be the housing chair and I’m not lobbying to be the housing chair,” the Manhattan lawmaker said. “Several other people have voiced active interest and I think that’s great.”

“I actually think that whoever is willing to be the housing chair should recognize they need to probably make a six-year commitment to this assignment,” she added. “And I’m not actually planning necessarily to make an additional six-year commitment to the Senate.”
body_zh: 享有（临时）福利的朋友：纽约市市长佐兰·马姆达尼（Zohran Mamdani）公布了他与唐纳德·特朗普总统的亲密关系的最新福利，并于今天宣布了一项协议，该协议将给全国各地的商店更多时间来遵守联邦食品援助规则的变化。
农业部上周生效的新规定要求零售商储存更多种类的产品，以便继续获得 SNAP 福利。
就在他们开始实施之前，马姆达尼签署了一封两党致美国农业部部长布鲁克·罗林斯的信，敦促特朗普政府推迟实施新​​要求。他警告说，如果这些商店不能及时满足要求并失去接受 SNAP 付款的能力，这些规定将威胁到该市 10,000 多家酒窖和街角商店以及依赖它们的纽约人的生存能力。
现在，在与罗林斯和曾是敌人的兄弟特朗普谈判后，马姆达尼为小型零售商争取了 90 天的延期，以遵守这些规定——不仅是在纽约市，而且是在全国范围内。延期从周五开始。
马姆达尼表示，在市政厅与联邦政府联系后，他亲自向特朗普总统提出了延期请求。
他说：“我告诉总统的是，这项规定如果允许按计划的时间表实施，将会使众多纽约工薪阶层的生活陷入真正的焦虑和混乱。” “总统认真对待了这一担忧。”
马姆达尼拒绝透露他与特朗普聊天的频率——“我会保持我们两人之间的聊天节奏，”他说——但他强调他们的对话正在进行中。
在两位高管即将迎来他们意外的兄弟情谊一周年之际，今天的声明提醒人们，马姆达尼的特朗普战略已基本获得回报。
11 月 21 日，在两人首次椭圆形办公室会面后，看似陷入爱情的特朗普出现后，与明尼阿波利斯市相当的移民执法激增的威胁基本上消失了，消除了当时笼罩在市长上任初期的潜在爆炸性局势。
今年二月，马姆达尼成功请求特朗普释放一名被美国移民和海关执法局拘留的哥伦比亚大学学生，正如《政治》杂志本周报道的那样，马姆达尼继续私下向总统提出这些请求。两人还讨论了联邦政府参与一项横跨皇后区 Sunnyside Yard 火车站的大型开发项目。
到目前为止，这些战利品的价格是马姆达尼的基地愿意接受的价格。
市长很少（如果有的话）直接批评特朗普。当记者询问他们的私人电话时，他表示反对。 9月底，在格雷西大厦外联合露面时，当被问及特朗普短暂的白宫媒体禁令时，马姆达尼仅表示，他本人支持各种新闻媒体报道市政厅。 — 莫莉·莱因曼和乔·阿努塔
NVIDIA 及其他领域：州长 Kathy Hochul 并不担心 Nvidia 前首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 的丑闻会影响更广泛的半导体行业。
“这是一个有弹性的行业，”她今天表示。 “我们已经在从马耳他一直到锡拉丘兹的地方插上了旗帜。纽约的经济将继续健康并继续增长。这不会影响我们履行继续投资和创造更多就业机会的义务。”
纽约对该行业下了巨大的长期赌注，该行业在锡拉丘兹地区和马耳他萨拉托加县小镇立足，霍赫尔今天在当地宣传了新芯片制造工厂的破土动工。

科技繁荣帮助提振了华尔街并增加了纽约的金库。经济放缓可能会给经济带来麻烦。 — 尼克·赖斯曼

这位曼哈顿议员表示：“我不会担任住房委员会主席，也不会游说担任住房委员会主席。” “其他几个人也表达了积极的兴趣，我认为这很好。”

body_en: Maryland senator’s bid against Chuck Schumer for leadership could decide direction of the Democratic party

Ever since Donald Trump returned to the White House, Democratic officeholders and voters alike have been divided over whether their leader in the Senate, Chuck Schumer , is up to the task of taking the president on.

That debate intensified on Thursday, when the Maryland senator Chris Van Hollen announced he will challenge Schumer for the post of Democratic Senate leader, which will become one of the most powerful jobs in Washington when the party takes control of Congress ’s upper chamber next year.

The contest between Schumer and Van Hollen is the party’s first major test of unity after its triumph in last week’s midterm elections, in which voters gave Democrats their biggest majorities in both the Senate and House of Representatives in years. Now the party will be forced to confront the two veteran lawmakers’ differing visions on how to use their newly expanded power to confront Trump, advance the party’s agenda and address divisive issues such as the question of aid to Israel.
Who is Chris Van Hollen? The senator challenging Schumer as a progressive voice for Democrats

“Trump’s policies have been fired, but we are still in the position where we need to take advantage of this opportunity. So that does mean closing the trust deficit? … And I don’t think you can close the trust deficit by simply returning to the status quo,” Van Hollen said at a press conference on Friday.

Progressive groups have cheered the 67-year-old Van Hollen’s candidacy, and he’s picked up a handful of endorsements in the hours since he made his bid official. But his prospects are unclear: the senator said he is an “underdog” in the contest, which is set to be decided at a behind-closed-doors caucus meeting scheduled for 1 December.
Schumer, meanwhile, has expressed confidence he’ll win the Democratic caucus’s nod again, and has the support of senators from across the party’s ideological spectrum.

“I welcome any discussion about the future of our caucus and the important work ahead,” Schumer, 75, wrote on X after Van Hollen announced his bid. “I have the votes to continue serving as Democratic Leader.”

A New York City native, Schumer won election to the House in 1980, then the Senate in 1998. He became the top Senate Democrat in 2017, when the party was in the minority at the beginning of Trump’s first term. Four years later, Schumer became majority leader under Joe Biden, and managed to win passage of parts of his legislative agenda even though the Democratic caucus was so small it could not lose a single vote on party-line bills.

Trump returned to power in 2025, and it was not long after that Schumer’s leadership came into question. In March of that year, Congress faced a deadline to approve new government funding or cause a shutdown. Though many Democrats believed they had leverage over Trump to win concessions , perhaps over the gutting of the federal government by the “department of government efficiency”, Schumer opted to advance a GOP-backed spending measure, arguing that it was a bad time to shut down the government.

The compromise triggered an explosion of anger at Schumer both from Democrats in the House of Representatives who had rejected the funding compromise, and activist groups who saw it as a sign that Schumer was no longer fit to be leader.

“Senator Schumer has contributed to and led many important accomplishments that Indivisible is grateful for. But with our democracy on the line, he let us, the country and the Democratic party down,” said Ezra Levin, co-executive director of the network of progressive groups.
“Senator Schumer should step aside as leader. Every Democrat in the Senate should call for him to do so, and begin making plans for new leadership immediately.”

The relationship between Schumer and the party base – including some Democratic lawmakers – has yet to recover. Another wave of calls for Schumer to step down arrived later that year, when dissident Senate Democrats decided to end a record-long government shutdown without Republicans meeting any of their demands on healthcare.

Schumer did not publicly endorse their deal, but it was widely believed to have his backing. By the time campaigning for the 2026 midterms began, several candidates were making their opposition to him prominent in their platforms.

In some ways, the tension is a unique consequence of the differences in power between the minority party in the House and Senate. In the former, the party out of power has little recourse to block legislation, but in the latter, the filibuster’s 60-vote threshold makes Schumer a major figure in deciding whether his party plays along with the 53 Republicans in the majority, or obstructs them.

At the same time that Schumer’s standing among Democrats was growing rocky, Van Hollen’s star was ascending. Elected to the Senate from the House in 2016, Van Hollen made national news when he traveled to El Salvador to meet Kilmar Ábrego García, a Salvadorian who had been wrongfully deported from Maryland in the early days of Trump’s mass deportation campaign.

He has joined in criticizing Israel, amid a wider backlash among Democratic voters towards the US ally fueled by accusations it committed a genocide in Gaza. Van Hollen voted against providing bulldozers and bombs to the country, and after a visit to the Gaza-Egypt border in 2025, co-released a report accusing Israel of planning to ethnically cleanse the territory. In September, the senator led an unsuccessful resolution to force the state department to issue a report on violence in the West Bank.
body_zh: 马里兰州参议员与查克·舒默争夺领导权可能会决定民主党的方向
自从唐纳德·特朗普重返白宫以来，民主党官员和选民对于参议院领袖查克·舒默是否能胜任总统的任务一直存在分歧。
周四，这场辩论愈演愈烈，马里兰州参议员克里斯·范·霍伦宣布，他将挑战舒默担任民主党参议院领袖一职，当该党明年控制国会上议院时，这将成为华盛顿最有权势的职位之一。
舒默和范霍伦之间的竞争是民主党在上周中期选举中获胜后首次对团结进行重大考验，选民让民主党在参议院和众议院获得了多年来的最大多数席位。现在，该党将被迫面对两位资深议员的不同愿景，即如何利用他们新扩大的权力来对抗特朗普、推进该党的议程以及解决对以色列的援助问题等分裂问题。
克里斯·范霍伦是谁？参议员挑战舒默作为民主党的进步声音
范霍伦在周五的新闻发布会上表示：“特朗普的政策已经被取消，但我们仍然需要利用这个机会。那么这是否意味着消除信任赤字？……而且我不认为仅仅通过恢复现状就可以消除信任赤字。”
进步团体对 67 岁的范霍伦的候选资格表示欢迎，自他正式竞选后的几个小时内，他就获得了一些支持。但他的前景尚不明朗：这位参议员表示，他在这场竞选中处于“劣势”，这场竞选将在定于 12 月 1 日举行的闭门核心小组会议上决定。
与此同时，舒默表示有信心再次赢得民主党核心小组的认可，并得到党内不同意识形态派别参议员的支持。
“我欢迎任何关于我们核心小组的未来和未来重要工作的讨论，”75 岁的舒默在范霍伦宣布竞选后在 X 上写道。 “我有票数继续担任民主党领袖。”
舒默是纽约人，1980 年赢得众议院选举，1998 年赢得参议院选举。2017 年，他成为参议院民主党领袖，当时该党在特朗普第一个任期之初处于少数派地位。四年后，舒默成为乔·拜登领导下的多数党领袖，并成功赢得了部分立法议程的通过，尽管民主党核心小组规模很小，在党派路线法案上不能失去任何一票。
特朗普于2025年重新掌权，不久之后舒默的领导力就受到质疑。同年 3 月，国会面临着批准新政府资金或导致政府关门的最后期限。尽管许多民主党人认为他们对特朗普有影响力以赢得让步，也许是因为“政府效率部”对联邦政府的破坏，但舒默选择推进共和党支持的支出措施，认为现在不是关闭政府的糟糕时机。
这一妥协引发了对舒默的愤怒，众议院的民主党人拒绝了资金妥协，而激进团体则认为这是舒默不再适合担任领导人的迹象。
进步团体网络联合执行主任埃兹拉·莱文表示：“舒默参议员为许多重要成就做出了贡献并领导了不可分割的感激之情。但随着我们的民主岌岌可危，他让我们、国家和民主党失望了。”
“舒默参议员应该辞去领导人职务。参议院的每一位民主党人都应该呼吁他这样做，并立即开始制定新领导层的计划。”
舒默与党内基础 — — 包括一些民主党议员 — — 之间的关系尚未恢复。同年晚些时候，另一波要求舒默下台的呼声到来，当时持不同政见的参议院民主党人决定结束创纪录的政府关门，而共和党人则没有满足他们对医疗保健的任何要求。
舒默没有公开支持他们的协议，但人们普遍认为得到了他的支持。当 2026 年中期选举的竞选活动开始时，几位候选人在他们的政纲中突出地表达了对他的反对。
在某些方面，紧张局势是众议院和参议院少数党之间权力差异的独特后果。在前者中，下台的政党几乎没有办法阻止立法，但在后者中，阻挠议事的60票门槛使舒默成为决定他的政党是与占多数的53名共和党人合作还是阻碍他们的主要人物。
与此同时，舒默在民主党中的地位日渐岌岌可危，范霍伦的星光却在冉冉升起。 2016 年，范霍伦从众议院当选为参议员，他前往萨尔瓦多会见萨尔瓦多人基尔马·阿布雷戈·加西亚 (Kilmar Ábrego García)，他在特朗普大规模驱逐运动初期被错误地从马里兰州驱逐出境，成为全国新闻。
他也加入了对以色列的批评之际，民主党选民对这个美国盟友的强烈反对情绪因以色列在加沙实施种族灭绝的指控而加剧。范霍伦投票反对向该国提供推土机和炸弹，并在 2025 年访问加沙-埃及边境后，共同发布了一份报告，指责以色列计划对该地区进行种族清洗。 9月，这位参议员主导了一项迫使国务院发布有关约旦河西岸暴力事件报告的决议，但没有成功。

summary_zh: 七名美国人对 43 岁的科洛姆寄予厚望，他是自重建民主党人斯科特·科洛姆本月创造历史以来密西西比州第一位黑人参议员
body_en: Seven Americans on their hopes for Colom, 43, Mississippi’s first Black senator since Reconstruction
Democrat Scott Colom made history this month, becoming Mississippi’s first Black senator since the Reconstruction era after defeating incumbent Republican senator Cindy Hyde-Smith.
The 43-year-old’s win also contributed to a Democratic majority of at least 55 seats in the Senate – the party’s largest midterm gains since 1986.

Voters across the US reflected on the significance of Colom’s victory, with many older voters expressing hope that it could signal a new chapter for a state and region marked by a long history of racism and segregation. Others looked to Colom and a new generation of Democrats to deliver on key campaign promises, from tackling the cost of living and ending the US war with Iran to addressing the Trump administration’s hardline immigration policies.

Dye Bailey, a Black older adult in Grenada, Mississippi , said: “It makes me so proud to see Scott Colom win the Senate because Mississippi has been trying to [prevent] Black people from voting for our rights for so long. Mississippi is so racist, but I’m proud that all [of] Mississippi can [come] together as one people.”
Bailey added that she hopes Colom will fight for healthcare for all Mississippians, “feed[ing] the needy” and protect voting rights.
For Greg P, a 71-year old retired professor based in Chicago who spent most of his childhood and young adulthood in Mississippi, Colom’s victory offers hope.

“My father was an Episcopal priest, and my family was active in the civil rights movement in the 1960s and 70s. Our family had a cross burned into our rectory’s front lawn in 1971, and I was assaulted several times in my mid-teens by racists incensed by our activism,” he said.

“What gives me hope is that Colom was able to speak to Black and white Mississippians, convincing Black voters that this time they could actually win, and persuading a significant percentage of whites that a Black senator would actually do better by them than a white one had for years.”

He continued: “Whites in Mississippi would often tell me of the awful things they believed would happen to them ‘if the Blacks ever take over’, showing an absolute clarity about what whites had done to Black people there over the decades and centuries. They believed that revenge would be the first order of business. Now, it appears that a significant number of them have overcome that fear, which gives me great hope that others will come along that way in the future.”

Like Greg, Catherine Park, a 64-year-old hospital lab director based in Newark, Delaware, sees Colom’s victory as a sign of change. Park grew up in south Mississippi in the 1970s, when the “KKK was a real presence in the state”.

“I am so proud and excited for senator Colom. I have been watching the news daily over his growing lead. The times they are a’ changin’,” Park said. She added that she hoped he “makes a difference in one of the nation’s poorest states” and that “his example becomes a shining light to bring Mississippi out of the 19th century and into the 21st”.

Pat Crimm, a 72-year-old retired electrical engineer who grew up in Jackson, Mississippi, during the segregation era, said that he registered to vote on his 18th birthday, casting his first ballot against Richard Nixon. He sees Colom’s victory as ushering in a new political chapter for Mississippi.

“Besides Dixiecrats, I have only voted for one Democrat who carried Mississippi and was elected – Jimmy Carter,” Crimm said, adding: “Scott Colom seems like a good man who will help us recover from the current administration. His predecessor in the Senate was against poor people and an ardent Maga. My hope is that there is a new sheriff in town who will fight for Mississippi and America.”

For Sherri Vacarella, a 75-year-old retired teacher based in Portland, Oregon, who grew up in Alabama during the 1950s and 1960s, Colom’s victory “is the most exciting change in southern politics in my long lifetime”.

“The idea that he will represent Mississippi, a state that has tried to prevent Black representation since Reconstruction, is particularly sweet to this progressive Democrat elder. I pray for his success and fully expect he’ll do an excellent job as Senator of Mississippi,” she said. “I’m optimistic that senator Colom will focus on affordability and offer legislation that will reduce costs and provide a more trustworthy national government, putting an end to ICE horrors, the Iran war, and Pete Hegseth.”

Similarly, JJ Amaworo Wilson, a 57-year-old writer based in New Mexico who identifies as Anglo-Nigerian-American, said: “In the most racist state in a deeply racist country, this is an extraordinary result, a seismic shift. In the arena of modern electoral politics, it’s comparable only to [Barack] Obama’s ascension to the presidency. Colom knows his history. He knows his achievement comes in the aftermath of the civil rights struggle of Fannie Lou Hamer, Martin Luther King, John Lewis, and many others.”

Wilson continued: “Colom has earned his place in history. Now he must focus on the present, particularly the cost of living and corruption. I hope he succeeds in improving the lives of everyone in Mississippi, including those who voted against him, because that’s his mandate and that’s how he’ll stay in office.”

Charmaine Rehg, 74, who lives in Eugene, Oregon, and is originally from St Louis, Missouri, said Colom’s victory will “mean much more respect for Mississippi, which has been belittled for being ‘backwards’ and ‘redneck’”.
body_zh: 七名美国人对 43 岁的科罗姆寄予厚望，科罗姆是密西西比州重建以来第一位黑人参议员
民主党人斯科特·科洛姆本月创造了历史，击败现任共和党参议员辛迪·海德·史密斯后，成为密西西比州自重建时代以来第一位黑人参议员。
这位 43 岁的候选人的胜利还帮助民主党在参议院获得了至少 55 个席位，这是该党自 1986 年以来中期选举中取得的最大胜利。
美国各地的选民反思了科罗姆胜利的意义，许多年长选民表示希望这能为一个长期存在种族主义和种族隔离历史的州和地区开启新的篇章。其他人则指望科罗姆和新一代民主党人兑现关键的竞选承诺，从解决生活成本问题、结束美国与伊朗的战争，到解决特朗普政府的强硬移民政策。
密西西比州格林纳达的一名黑人老年人戴伊·贝利 (Dye Bailey) 说：“看到斯科特·科洛姆赢得参议院让我感到非常自豪，因为密西西比州长期以来一直试图[阻止]黑人为我们的权利投票。密西西比州是如此种族主义，但我很自豪密西西比州所有人都能作为一个民族[团结起来]。”
贝利补充说，她希望科罗姆为所有密西西比人的医疗保健而奋斗，“养活有需要的人”并保护投票权。
71 岁的芝加哥退休教授格雷格·P (Greg P) 在密西西比州度过了童年和青年时期的大部分时间，对于他来说，科罗姆的胜利带来了希望。
“我的父亲是一名圣公会牧师，我的家人积极参与 20 世纪 60 年代和 70 年代的民权运动。1971 年，我们家在教区长官邸前的草坪上烧了一个十字架，我在十几岁的时候就多次遭到因我们的激进主义而激怒的种族主义者的袭击，”他说。
“给我带来希望的是，科罗姆能够与密西西比黑人和白人交谈，让黑人选民相信这一次他们实际上可以获胜，并说服很大一部分白人，黑人参议员实际上会比白人参议员多年来为他们做得更好。”
他继续说：“密西西比州的白人经常告诉我，他们认为‘如果黑人接管’，他们会发生可怕的事情，这表明他们绝对清楚地了解了几十年来、几个世纪以来白人对那里的黑人所做的事情。他们相信复仇将是首要任务。现在，他们中的很多人似乎已经克服了这种恐惧，这给了我很大的希望，希望其他人在未来也能走上这条路。”
与格雷格一样，特拉华州纽瓦克市 64 岁的医院实验室主任凯瑟琳·帕克 (Catherine Park) 也将科罗姆的胜利视为变革的标志。帕克于 20 世纪 70 年代在密西西比州南部长大，当时“三K党在该州真正存在”。
“我为科罗姆参议员感到骄傲和兴奋。我每天都在关注他不断增长的领先优势的新闻。时代正在‘改变’，”帕克说。她补充说，她希望他“为美国最贫穷的州之一带来改变”，并且“他的榜样成为一盏明灯，带领密西西比州走出 19 世纪，进入 21 世纪”。
帕特·克里姆 (Pat Crimm) 是一位 72 岁的退休电气工程师，在种族隔离时期在密西西比州杰克逊长大。他说，他在 18 岁生日那天登记投票，投下了第一张选票，反对理查德·尼克松 (Richard Nixon)。他认为科罗姆的胜利开启了密西西比州新的政治篇章。
克里姆说：“除了迪克西克拉特人之外，我只投票给了一位赢得密西西比州并当选的民主党人——吉米·卡特。”他补充道：“斯科特·科罗姆似乎是一个好人，他将帮助我们从现任政府中恢复过来。他在参议院的前任反对穷人和热心的马加。我希望镇上有一位新的警长，他将为密西西比州和美国而战。”
雪莉·瓦卡雷拉 (Sherri Vacarella) 是俄勒冈州波特兰市一位 75 岁的退休教师，她于 20 世纪 50 年代和 1960 年代在阿拉巴马州长大，对于她来说，科罗姆的胜利“是我漫长一生中南方政治中最激动人心的变化”。
“他将代表密西西比州，这个州自重建以来一直试图阻止黑人代表，这一想法对这位进步的民主党元老来说特别甜蜜。我为他的成功祈祷，并完全期待他作为密西西比州参议员的出色工作，”她说。 “我乐观地认为，科洛姆参议员将关注负担能力，并提出立法，以降低成本并提供一个更值得信赖的国家政府，结束 ICE 的恐怖、伊朗战争和皮特·赫格斯。”
同样，来自新墨西哥州的 57 岁作家、英裔尼日利亚裔美国人 J·J·阿马沃罗·威尔逊 (JJ Amaworo Wilson) 表示：“在种族主义最严重的国家中，这是一个非同寻常的结果，是一个巨大的转变。在现代选举政治的舞台上，这只能与[巴拉克]奥巴马当选总统相媲美。科罗姆了解他的历史。他知道他的成就是在民权运动之后取得的。范妮·卢·哈默、马丁·路德·金、约翰·刘易斯和许多其他人的奋斗。”
威尔逊继续说道：“科罗姆已经在历史上赢得了自己的一席之地。现在他必须关注当下，特别是生活成本和腐败。我希望他成功地改善密西西比州每个人的生活，包括那些投票反对他的人，因为这是他的使命，也是他留任的方式。”
现年 74 岁的 Charmaine Rehg 来自密苏里州圣路易斯，居住在俄勒冈州尤金市，她表示科罗姆的胜利将“意味着对密西西比州更加尊重，因为密西西比州一直被贬低为‘落后’和‘乡巴佬’”。

title_en: Mamdani and Trump agree to 90-day delay on new food assistance rules for corner stores
title_zh: 马姆达尼和特朗普同意将街角商店的新食品援助规则推迟 90 天
summary: New York City mayor says deal will allow bodegas and convenience stores across the country more time to comply Zohran Mamdani, the New York City mayor, has struck a deal with Donald Trump to secure a 90-day delay on new rules for the Supplemental Nutrition Ass
summary_zh: 纽约市市长表示，该协议将使全国各地的酒窖和便利店有更多时间遵守纽约市市长佐兰·马姆达尼 (Zohran Mamdani) 的规定
body_en: Mamdani and Trump agree to 90-day delay on new food assistance rules for corner stores | Zohran Mamdani
New York City mayor says deal will allow bodegas and convenience stores across the country more time to comply

Zohran Mamdani, the New York City mayor, has struck a deal with Donald Trump to secure a 90-day delay on new rules for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (Snap), so that bodegas and corner stores across the country have time to comply.
The extension, Mamdani said, starts Friday as a result of conversations he had with Trump and Brooke Rollins, the agriculture secretary.

The new guidelines, implemented by the US agriculture department, which retailers would have had to meet by 4 November, require stores to stock at least seven varieties within each staple food category: dairy, grains, protein and fruits or vegetables. Retailers would also have to ensure that they offer perishable items in three of the staple food categories.
The new guidelines threw the lives of “more than a million New Yorkers” and “tens of milllions more across America” into “chaos”, the mayor said at a press conference on Friday.

“People already reckoning with a shortage of affordable places to buy what they need for their home, soaring costs at the register, and food deserts across the five boroughs, now feared that the few places they could shop would no longer be able to accept their benefits,” Mamdani said.

Several advocates were concerned that the new rules would mean people relying on Snap would be unable to buy groceries at their only accessible store. According to the Food Research and Action Center, bodegas, convenience stores and small grocery stores make up roughly 70% of Snap retailers.
Given the tight timeframe to adjust their stock and meet the new requirements, small retailers ran the risk of going out of business if they couldn’t accept Snap benefits, the mayor said.
“For so many of our fellow Americans, whether they shop at a general store in Michigan or a convenience store in Missouri, would have struggled to use their benefits and feed those they love.”

More than 100 bodega owners reached out to Mamdani’s office with concerns about the new rule. According to the New York City department of city planning, there are more than 10,000 bodegas and corner stores across the five boroughs.
body_zh: 马姆达尼和特朗普同意将街角商店的新食品援助规则推迟 90 天佐兰·马姆达尼
纽约市市长表示，该协议将使全国各地的杂货店和便利店有更多时间遵守规定
纽约市市长佐兰·马姆达尼 (Zohran Mamdani) 与唐纳德·特朗普 (Donald Trump) 达成协议，确保将补充营养援助计划 (Snap) 的新规定推迟 90 天，以便全国各地的酒窖和街角商店有时间遵守。
马姆达尼表示，由于他与特朗普和农业部长布鲁克·罗林斯进行了交谈，延期将于周五开始。
美国农业部实施的新指导方针要求商店在每个主食类别中至少储备七个品种：乳制品、谷物、蛋白质和水果或蔬菜，零售商必须在 11 月 4 日之前遵守该指导方针。零售商还必须确保他们提供三种主食类别的易腐烂商品。
市长在周五的新闻发布会上表示，新的指导方针使“超过一百万纽约人”和“全美数千万人”的生活陷入“混乱”。
马姆达尼说：“人们已经意识到缺乏负担得起的地方来购买他们的家庭所需的东西，收银台的成本飙升，以及五个行政区的食品沙漠，现在担心他们可以购物的少数地方将不再能够接受他们的福利。”
一些倡导者担心，新规定将意味着依赖 Snap 的人们将无法在他们唯一可以进入的商店购买食品杂货。根据食品研究与行动中心的数据，酒窖、便利店和小型杂货店约占 Snap 零售商的 70%。
市长表示，鉴于调整库存和满足新要求的时间紧迫，小型零售商如果不能接受 Snap 福利，就会面临倒闭的风险。
“对于我们许多美国同胞来说，无论他们是在密歇根州的杂货店还是密苏里州的便利店购物，都很难利用他们的福利并养活他们所爱的人。”
超过 100 名酒窖老板联系了 Mamdani 的办公室，对新规定表示担忧。据纽约市城市规划部门称，五个行政区共有超过 10,000 家酒窖和街角商店。

title_en: The Trump administration's voter roll crusade could continue
title_zh: 特朗普政府的选民名册运动可能会继续
summary: Election officials are preparing for the Trump administration's pressure tactics over potential noncitizens on state voter rolls to continue, though recent court rulings pose new obstacles.
summary_zh: 选举官员正在为特朗普政府继续对州选民名册上的潜在非公民采取施压策略做准备，尽管
body_en: Election workers process vote-by-mail ballots at the Los Angeles County Ballot Processing Center on Nov. 5. Mario Tama/Getty Images hide caption

In the weeks before Election Day, the Trump administration escalated its hunt for voter fraud and its pressure on election officials — especially in California — to crack down on illegal voting by non-U.S. citizens.

Now, with Election Day come and gone, election officials and civil rights attorneys are preparing for the administration to continue its search for noncitizens on state voter rolls, as well as what they see as intimidation tactics toward election officials.

"It's clear that there is this drive to try to conjure up facts that just don't exist. I don't think that's going to change," James Williams, county executive for California's Santa Clara County, told NPR. "So we fully are prepared to continue to deal with this."

In recent weeks, federal prosecutors announced criminal charges against dozens of people who are accused of voting or registering to vote without being a citizen. Yet compared to overall numbers of voters, noncitizen voting is exceptionally rare . And since summer, the administration has touted what turned out to be grossly inflated numbers of noncitizens on state voter rolls.
Tens of millions cast ballots for midterms despite worries of Trump's interference

In mid-October, federal officials alleged they had found 20,000 "likely" noncitizens on California's voter rolls. The Department of Justice sued the state to try to force election officials not to count ballots of voters whose citizenship had not been verified. A federal judge and a federal appeals court rejected the DOJ's requests , and the U.S. Supreme Court declined to intervene .

In the days leading up to Election Day, with the lawsuit pending, U.S. attorneys in California sent grand jury subpoenas to several counties, asking for records related to how local officials responded to DOJ's demands.
Though DOJ dropped its lawsuit last week, it has not rescinded these subpoenas.

"We have ongoing cases and investigations in various states surrounding voter process," U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche said at a Thursday press conference. "We are actively, and will continue to investigate election integrity cases criminally and civilly, and that wasn't expected to start or stop — no matter what the results of the election were last week."
But recent unfavorable rulings for the Trump administration have created new obstacles for future federal attempts to intervene on state voter list maintenance.

"Do I think they will still keep at this? I do, but there are just a lot of court losses that are going to be really difficult for them to maneuver around," Anna Baldwin, director of voting rights litigation at Campaign Legal Center, told NPR. "They've hit substantial roadblocks because it's a lawless program that Congress has never authorized."
Recent court orders reaffirmed that states have the authority to run their elections and called into question the credibility of the federal government's data on noncitizens.

One key ruling , which came down the night before Election Day, found that DOJ and the Department of Homeland Security lack any statutory authority to distribute lists of purported noncitizens to election officials. In that order, a federal judge in Washington, D.C., wrote that taking that action also violates the Privacy Act. The federal government could appeal.

In an earlier order in October , a different D.C.-based judge vacated the DOJ's project of requesting unredacted voter rolls from states, seeking to compare that voter data to federal databases, and instructing states to remove suspected noncitizens. The ruling found those actions were unlawful and disenfranchised eligible voters. The DOJ has appealed.

The Department of Justice declined to comment on litigation or future plans, but said in a statement, "The Department will continue to enforce federal election laws and will evaluate matters based on the facts and the law."
Looming criminal proceedings and subpoenas to election officials

Federal prosecutors have vowed to continue tracking down noncitizen voting cases, as have some local prosecutors. San Luis Obispo District Attorney Dan Dow is investigating the potential noncitizen voters federal officials flagged in his county. He has so far charged one individual.
"It has always been a crime but I've never had a noncitizen case referred to me. When we got 63 of them, we said, 'We will look at them,'" Dow told NPR. "It is our duty to uphold California law."
body_zh: 11 月 5 日，选举工作人员在洛杉矶县选票处理中心处理邮寄选票。Mario Tama/Getty Images 隐藏标题栏
在选举日前几周，特朗普政府加大了对选民欺诈的追捕力度，并向选举官员（尤其是加州官员）施压，要求其打击非美国公民的非法投票。
现在，随着选举日的临近，选举官员和民权律师正在为政府继续寻找州选民名册上的非公民以及他们认为对选举官员的恐吓策略做准备。
加利福尼亚州圣克拉拉县县长詹姆斯·威廉姆斯 (James Williams) 告诉美国国家公共广播电台 (NPR)，“很明显，人们试图虚构出不存在的事实。我认为这种情况不会改变。” “所以我们完全准备好继续处理这个问题。”
最近几周，联邦检察官宣布对数十名被指控在非公民身份下投票或登记投票的人提出刑事指控。然而，与选民总数相比，非公民投票的情况异常罕见。自夏季以来，政府一直在宣传州选民名册上的非公民人数，结果发现其数量严重夸大。
尽管担心特朗普的干涉，仍有数千万人为中期选举投票
十月中旬，联邦官员声称他们在加州选民名册上发现了 20,000 名“可能”的非公民。司法部起诉该州，试图迫使选举官员不统计公民身份未经核实的选民的选票。一名联邦法官和联邦上诉法院拒绝了司法部的请求，美国最高法院也拒绝干预。
在选举日之前的几天里，随着诉讼悬而未决，加州的美国检察官向几个县发出了大陪审团传票，要求提供与当地官员如何回应司法部要求有关的记录。
尽管司法部上周撤销了诉讼，但并未撤销这些传票。
美国司法部长托德·布兰奇在周四的新闻发布会上表示：“我们在各州正在进行有关选民程序的案件和调查。” “我们正在积极并将继续对选举诚信案件进行刑事和民事调查，无论上周的选举结果如何，预计调查都不会开始或停止。”
但最近对特朗普政府不利的裁决为联邦未来干预州选民名单维护的尝试制造了新的障碍。

"Do I think they will still keep at this? I do, but there are just a lot of court losses that are going to be really difficult for them to maneuver around," Anna Baldwin, director of voting rights litigation at Campaign Legal Center, told NPR. “他们遇到了巨大的障碍，因为这是国会从未授权的无法无天的计划。”
最近的法院命令重申各州有权进行选举，并对联邦政府非公民数据的可信度提出质疑。
选举日前一天晚上做出的一项关键裁决发现，司法部和国土安全部没有任何法定权力向选举官员分发所谓的非公民名单。华盛顿特区的一名联邦法官在该命令中写道，采取这一行动也违反了《隐私法》。联邦政府可以上诉。
在 10 月份的一项早些时候的命令中，另一位华盛顿特区的法官撤销了司法部要求各州提供未经编辑的选民名单的项目，寻求将选民数据与联邦数据库进行比较，并指示各州删除可疑的非公民。裁决发现这些行为是非法的，并且剥夺了合格选民的选举权。美国司法部已提出上诉。
司法部拒绝就诉讼或未来计划发表评论，但在一份声明中表示，“司法部将继续执行联邦选举法，并将根据事实和法律评估此事。”
迫在眉睫的刑事诉讼和对选举官员的传票
联邦检察官发誓要继续追查非公民投票案件，一些地方检察官也是如此。圣路易斯奥比斯波地区检察官丹·道正在调查联邦官员在他所在县标记的潜在非公民选民。到目前为止，他已对一人提出指控。
“这一直是犯罪行为，但我从来没有收到过向我转介的非公民案件。当我们收到 63 起案件时，我们说，‘我们会关注他们，’”陶告诉 NPR。 “维护加州法律是我们的责任。”

title_en: New Orleans boat crash live: all passengers and crew found alive in ‘miracle on the Mississippi’
title_zh: 新奥尔良沉船事故直播：“密西西比河上的奇迹”中所有乘客和船员都活着
summary: New Orleans mayor says 32 people are being treated for minor injuries after ship narrowly missed striking a major bridge Tanker collides with cruise ship on Mississippi River in New Orleans A video circulating around social media shows a different angle during
summary_zh: 新奥尔良市长表示，油轮险些撞上一座大桥，油轮与游轮相撞，造成 32 人轻伤，正在接受治疗
body_en: A tanker collided with a river cruise liner, the American Cruise Lines’ American Heritage, carrying 129 passengers plus crew in New Orleans on Friday. It began turning on its side and taking on water.
All passengers and crew are alive and have now been accounted for in what New Orleans mayor Helena Moreno called “truly a miracle on the Mississippi.”

It is unclear exactly what caused the collision. Melanie Burnham, commander of the US Coast Guard sector in New Orleans, told reporters that “there seems to be some type of a loss of steering,” in regards to the tanker.
Louisiana governor Jeff Landry, addressing reporters during a news conference, said he will be launching an investigation into what led to the collision to ensure it will not happen again.
Moreno said the tanker ship narrowly missed striking a bridge carrying around 160,000 vehicles daily.
Thirty-two people are being treated at a local hospital. Those include two New Orleans Harbor Police officers who went into the water to rescue people after the cruise ship began sinking.

Several photos and videos circulating around social media show different angles during the moment the ship was falling on its side into the water. Passengers were seen climbing onto the balconies’ railing to avoid sliding into the river as the ship turned horizontally.
body_zh: 周五，一艘油轮在新奥尔良与一艘载有 129 名乘客和船员的美国邮轮公司 American Heritage 游轮相撞。它开始侧翻并吸收水。
所有乘客和船员都还活着，现在已经找到了新奥尔良市长海伦娜·莫雷诺所说的“密西西比河上真正的奇迹”。
目前还不清楚到底是什么原因导致了这次碰撞。美国海岸警卫队驻新奥尔良部门指挥官梅兰妮·伯纳姆（Melanie Burnham）告诉记者，这艘油轮“似乎出现了某种类型的转向损失”。
路易斯安那州州长杰夫·兰德里在新闻发布会上向记者发表讲话时表示，他将对导致碰撞的原因展开调查，以确保此类事件不会再次发生。
莫雷诺表示，这艘油轮险些撞上了一座每天运载约 16 万辆汽车的桥梁。
三十二人正在当地一家医院接受治疗。其中包括两名新奥尔良港警察，他们在游轮开始下沉后潜入水中营救人员。
社交媒体上流传的几张照片和视频显示了这艘船侧身落入水中的那一刻的不同角度。当船水平转向时，乘客们爬上阳台的栏杆，以避免滑入河中。

title_en: Trump administration delays Medicaid work requirements by six months
title_zh: 特朗普政府将医疗补助工作要求推迟六个月
summary: Work requirements were set to go into effect on Jan. 1 for many able-bodied adults who receive Medicaid, which could have left millions without health insurance.
summary_zh: 工作要求将于 1 月 1 日对许多接受医疗补助的身体健全成年人生效，这可能导致数百万人失去健康
body_en: By Mike Hixenbaugh , Shannon Pettypiece and Elizabeth Chuck

The federal government on Friday announced a six-month delay in enforcing a Medicaid work requirement — a central provision in President Donald Trump’s “big, beautiful bill” that experts said would lead millions of Americans to lose health coverage.

The requirement still technically starts on Jan. 1, but under new guidance from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, states that choose not to enforce it won’t be held accountable until at least July 1.

The move is a striking turn for an administration that has spent months defending the policy against criticism from state officials and healthcare advocates who warned that the rollout was moving too quickly and that people who should be eligible for Medicaid would lose coverage because of the additional red tape and paperwork.

CMS called the six-month window a “hold harmless” period, and the delay is optional. States that choose to take advantage of this period will still start checking on Jan. 1 whether Medicaid enrollees are working, volunteering or in school or whether they qualify for an exemption. But until July, no one in those states will lose coverage for failing to meet the requirements.

“States have made real progress, and they’ve been clear with us about what it takes to get this right for beneficiaries — at scale and for the long term,” said Dan Brillman, who oversees Medicaid at CMS.
How Democrats intend to deliver on their big campaign promises

Some states have already moved forward with implementing the work requirements. In Nebraska, which launched the work requirements May 1, over 1,000 people have lost coverage or been denied benefits because of the new rules, according to state figures through August.

The Medicaid work requirement was a cornerstone of Trump’s “big, beautiful bill,” a massive tax and spending package that overwhelmingly benefited the wealthy through tax breaks while slashing the social safety net for vulnerable Americans. Millions of Americans are expected to lose health coverage and food assistance as a result of the law, the signature domestic legislation of Trump’s second term.

The law requires many able-bodied adults under the age of 65 to prove they work, volunteer or attend school at least 80 hours a month to keep Medicaid, which provides health coverage for low-income and disabled Americans. The Trump administration argues the requirement and other provisions in the law encourage work, reduce waste and protect government benefit programs for those who need them.

The Congressional Budget Office estimated the work requirements alone would leave 5.3 million more people uninsured by 2034 and would save the federal government $317 billion, part of nearly $1 trillion in Medicaid cuts in the law.

Pressure on the administration to delay the requirement had been building for months. Five Democratic governors last month asked Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. to postpone the implementation, saying that state agencies weren’t ready. And a federal judge last month blocked the Trump administration from enforcing a portion of the requirement related to medically frail people, saying it could lead some to wrongly lose coverage.
The delay comes a little more than a week after Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress on a promise to reverse the GOP’s cuts to healthcare and food assistance.

“Millions of people’s health care is at risk because of the Republican reconciliation law’s work requirement, as states scramble to implement on a rushed timeline & respond to shifting federal requirements,” Sarah Lueck, vice president for health policy at the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities, said in a post on X . “Today’s news lets states delay the harm.”
Mike Hixenbaugh is a senior investigative reporter for NBC News, based in Maryland, and author of "They Came for the Schools."
Shannon Pettypiece is senior policy reporter for NBC News.
Elizabeth Chuck is a reporter for NBC News who focuses on health and mental health, particularly issues that affect women and children.
body_zh: 作者：Mike Hixenbaugh、Shannon Pettypiece 和 Elizabeth Chuck
联邦政府周五宣布推迟执行医疗补助工作要求六个月，这是唐纳德·特朗普总统“大而美丽的法案”的核心条款，专家表示该条款将导致数百万美国人失去医疗保险。
从技术上讲，该要求仍从 1 月 1 日开始，但根据医疗保险和医疗补助服务中心的新指导，选择不执行该要求的人至少要到 7 月 1 日才会被追究责任。
对于政府来说，此举是一个惊人的转折，政府花了几个月的时间为该政策辩护，以应对州官员和医疗保健倡导者的批评，他们警告说，推出速度太快，应该有资格享受医疗补助的人将因额外的繁文缛节和文书工作而失去保险。
CMS 将六个月的窗口期称为“保持无害”期，并且延迟是可选的。选择利用这一时期的州仍将从 1 月 1 日开始检查医疗补助参与者是否在工作、志愿服务或在学校，或者他们是否有资格获得豁免。但直到七月份，这些州的任何人都不会因为不符合要求而失去保险。
CMS 医疗补助负责人丹·布里尔曼 (Dan Brillman) 表示：“各州已经取得了真正的进展，他们已经向我们明确表明需要采取哪些措施才能大规模、长期地为受益人提供这种权利。”
民主党打算如何兑现其重大竞选承诺
一些州已经开始实施工作要求。内布拉斯加州于 5 月 1 日推出了工作要求，根据截至 8 月份的州数据，已有 1,000 多人因新规定而失去保险或被拒绝领取福利。
医疗补助工作要求是特朗普“庞大而美丽的法案”的基石，这是一项庞大的税收和支出计划，通过税收减免使富人受益匪浅，同时削减了弱势美国人的社会安全网。这项法律是特朗普第二任期内标志性的国内立法，预计数百万美国人将失去医疗保险和食品援助。
该法律要求许多 65 岁以下身体健全的成年人证明他们每月工作、志愿或上学至少 80 小时，以保留为低收入和残疾人提供医疗保险的医疗补助计划。特朗普政府辩称，该要求和法律中的其他条款鼓励工作、减少浪费并保护为有需要的人提供的政府福利计划。
国会预算办公室估计，到 2034 年，仅工作要求一项就会导致 530 万人没有保险，并将为联邦政府节省 3,170 亿美元，这是法律中近 1 万亿美元医疗补助削减的一部分。
几个月来，政府一直面临着推迟这一要求的压力。上个月，五位民主党州长要求卫生部长小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪推迟实施，称州机构尚未准备好。上个月，一名联邦法官阻止特朗普政府执行与身体虚弱者相关的部分要求，称这可能会导致一些人错误地失去保险。
一周多前，民主党因承诺扭转共和党削减医疗保健和食品援助的政策而赢得了国会参众两院的控制权。
预算和政策优先事项中心负责卫生政策的副总裁萨拉·卢克 (Sarah Lueck) 在 X 上的一篇帖子中表示：“由于共和党和解法的工作要求，数百万人的医疗保健面临风险，因为各州都在匆忙的时间表内实施并应对不断变化的联邦要求。” “今天的新闻让各州推迟了伤害。”
迈克·希森博 (Mike Hixenbaugh) 是马里兰州 NBC 新闻的高级调查记者，也是《他们为学校而来》一书的作者。
Shannon Pettypiece 是 NBC 新闻的高级政策记者。
伊丽莎白·查克 (Elizabeth Chuck) 是 NBC 新闻的记者，专注于健康和心理健康，特别是影响妇女和儿童的问题。

title_en: These two voter turnout trends explain what happened across the South in the election
title_zh: 这两种选民投票率趋势解释了南方在选举中发生的情况
summary: In six states across the Deep South, a drastic swing to the left this election was driven by high Black voter turnout and compounded by a sharp decline in voting rates across Republican-heavy areas.
summary_zh: 在南部腹地的六个州，由于黑人选民投票率高，加上投票率急剧下降，导致这次选举急剧左倾。
body_en: A tale of 2 midterm election voter turnout trends in the South : NPR

A tale of 2 midterm election voter turnout trends in the South In six states across the Deep South, a drastic swing to the left this election was driven by high Black voter turnout and compounded by a sharp decline in voting rates across Republican-heavy areas.
Democratic victories in the South this year were driven just as much by who showed up to vote as who stayed home, according to an NPR analysis of turnout data.

Midterm elections normally have lower voter participation than presidential contests. But from Louisiana to the Carolinas, counties that voted for former Vice President Kamala Harris in 2024 came closer to matching — and in some cases exceeding — presidential turnout. At the same time, counties won by President Trump saw a much sharper decline in turnout and fewer Republican votes.

In six southern states — Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama, Georgia, South Carolina and North Carolina — turnout dropped by 19% in Harris-won counties compared to 26% in Trump-won counties. (In Louisiana, counties are called parishes.)
The South flexes political power in midterms, sets regional influence in 2028 election
Across the South, the six states analyzed swung an average of 22 points towards Democrats, larger than the national swing of about 14.5 points.

This differential turnout was a key factor in Democrats flipping Senate seats in North Carolina, South Carolina and Mississippi, and contributed to the closer-than-expected margin in Louisiana's Senate race.

In Mississippi, Democrat Scott Colom outperformed Harris, earning roughly 8,100 more votes than she did in 2024. Colom's margin over incumbent Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith is just over 5,600 votes as final ballots are being tallied.
Democratic Senate nominees in those six states earned more raw votes than Harris in 170 counties. On the flip side, the Republican nominees garnered hundreds of thousands fewer votes than Trump.

In special elections and primaries leading up to the midterms, voting data and polls showed a surge in Black voter participation, spurred in part by a Supreme Court decision that gutted part of the Voting Rights Act.

The Louisiana v. Callais decision led to changed congressional maps across the South, including Tennessee, Alabama, Louisiana and North Carolina. After redrawing boundary lines in a way that aimed to elect an 11-3 Republican majority delegation, North Carolina Democrats are now on track to hold an 11-3 majority.

Majority-Black counties overall had a higher voter turnout with about 85% compared to 76% for white, non-Hispanic majority counties. Sixteen majority-Black counties had more Democratic votes than during the 2024 election, with 12 of them in Mississippi. Clay County, Miss., had the largest voter turnout increase — by 17 points from 2024 to 2026.
Beyond majority-Black turnout, Democratic candidates in these southern states benefitted from a smaller drop in turnout from the 2024 election.

In Georgia, Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff finished with roughly 79,000 fewer votes than former Vice President Harris won in the state two years prior, despite there being more than a million fewer total votes overall.
The Democratic Party gained power across the country in the midterms. Now what?
All 159 counties in Georgia shifted toward Democrats. Ossoff flipped a dozen of them, including suburban Fayette County, on the way to a 14-point victory.

South Carolina had some of the largest Democratic voter turnout, with Greenville, Spartanburg and Lexington counties having the largest increases in raw Democratic votes from the 2024 election. Greenville, which backed Trump by 20 points two years ago, flipped to support Sen.-elect Annie Andrews by about 2 points.
body_zh: 南方两次中期选举选民投票率趋势的故事：NPR
南方两个中期选举选民投票率趋势的故事在南方腹地的六个州，由于黑人选民的高投票率以及共和党占多数地区的投票率急剧下降，导致这次选举出现了剧烈的左倾。
根据美国国家公共广播电台对投票率数据的分析，今年南方民主党的胜利既取决于谁去投票，也取决于谁留在家里。
中期选举的选民参与度通常低于总统竞选。但从路易斯安那州到卡罗莱纳州，2024 年投票给前副总统卡马拉·哈里斯的县的投票率更接近总统的投票率，在某些情况下甚至超过了总统的投票率。与此同时，特朗普总统获胜的县的投票率下降幅度更大，共和党选票也更少。
在路易斯安那州、密西西比州、阿拉巴马州、乔治亚州、南卡罗来纳州和北卡罗来纳州这六个南部州，哈里斯获胜县的投票率下降了 19%，而特朗普获胜县的投票率下降了 26%。 （在路易斯安那州，县被称为教区。）
南方在中期选举中展示政治权力，在 2028 年选举中确定地区影响力
在整个南方，所分析的六个州的支持率平均偏向民主党 22 个百分点，高于全国约 14.5 个百分点的偏向。
这种投票率差异是民主党在北卡罗来纳州、南卡罗来纳州和密西西比州翻转参议院席位的关键因素，并导致路易斯安那州参议员竞选的优势接近预期。
在密西西比州，民主党人斯科特·科洛姆(Scott Colom)的表现优于哈里斯，比2024年多获得约8,100张选票。随着最终选票的统计，科洛姆相对于现任共和党参议员辛迪·海德-史密斯(Cindy Hyde-Smith)的优势仅略高于5,600张选票。
这 6 个州的民主党参议院提名人获得的原始选票比哈里斯在 170 个县获得的原始选票还要多。另一方面，共和党提名人获得的选票比特朗普少数十万票。
在中期选举之前的特别选举和初选中，投票数据和民意调查显示，黑人选民的参与度大幅上升，部分原因是最高法院的一项裁决废除了《投票权法》的部分内容。
路易斯安那诉卡莱案的判决导致整个南方的国会地图发生变化，包括田纳西州、阿拉巴马州、路易斯安那州和北卡罗来纳州。在以 11-3 选举共和党多数派代表团的方式重新划定边界线后，北卡罗来纳州民主党现在有望以 11-3 占据多数席位。
总体而言，黑人占多数的县的选民投票率较高，约为 85%，而白人、非西班牙裔占多数的县的投票率为 76%。 16 个黑人占多数的县拥有比 2024 年选举期间更多的民主党选票，其中 12 个县位于密西西比州。密西西比州克莱县的选民投票率增幅最大，从 2024 年到 2026 年增加了 17 个百分点。
除了黑人占多数的投票率之外，这些南部各州的民主党候选人还受益于 2024 年大选投票率下降幅度较小。
在佐治亚州，民主党参议员乔恩·奥索夫(Jon Ossoff)最终获得的选票比两年前前副总统哈里斯在该州赢得的选票少了大约79,000张，尽管总选票总数减少了超过一百万张。
民主党在中期选举中在全国获得了权力。现在怎么办？
佐治亚州全部 159 个县都转向民主党。奥索夫击败了其中的十几个对手，其中包括费耶特县郊区，最终以 14 分的优势获胜。
南卡罗来纳州的民主党选民投票率最高，格林维尔、斯巴达堡和列克星敦县的民主党原始选票自 2024 年选举以来增幅最大。格林维尔两年前以 20 个百分点的支持率支持特朗普，现在却以大约 2 个百分点的支持率支持当选参议员安妮·安德鲁斯。

title_en: Trump's Justice Department faces a new era of scrutiny under a Democratic-led Congress
title_zh: 特朗普的司法部在民主党领导的国会下面临新时代的审查
summary: The Justice Department has functioned for nearly two years as an extension of the White House, unchecked by a Republican-controlled Congress
summary_zh: 司法部作为白宫的延伸部分运行了近两年，不受共和党控制的国会的限制
body_en: The Justice Department has functioned for nearly two years as an extension of the White House, unchecked by a Republican-controlled Congress
By ERIC TUCKER Associated Press and ALANNA DURKIN RICHER Associated Press

WASHINGTON -- The Justice Department has functioned for nearly two years as an extension of the White House, unchecked by a Republican-controlled Congress as it pursued investigations into President Donald Trump's enemies, fired waves of career employees and defended administration stances that judges across the country repeatedly deemed legally dubious .

Now, sweeping Democratic gains in Congress have shifted the balance of power in Washington, teeing up an onslaught of expected investigations into those actions and others as well as scrutiny from the majority party that the current Justice Department had until now managed to skirt.
The department has, at least publicly, appeared unbowed by the altered landscape.

Attorney General Todd Blanche says the department will cooperate with Congress but has also insisted that “we will not back down” from the Republican president's agenda. Meanwhile, a top aide told prosecutors on a call to prepare to be on “wartime” footing and a U.S. attorney publicly warned a top Democrat about planned congressional investigations.

It sets the stage for a pugilistic dynamic as Democrats promise to join already-skeptical courts in reining in the Trump administration while a Justice Department depleted by the losses of thousands of career employees and the postelection departures of senior leaders pledges to push ahead with its agenda.

Even though Democrats hold the gavel, they’re short on foolproof ways to guarantee Republican cooperation. Lawsuits can take years, subpoenas can be arduous to enforce and criminal contempt referrals for noncompliance would be sent to the Trump administration Justice Department, where they will almost certainly not be acted on.
“It’s a standoff and I don’t know what the answer to that is yet,” said Stan Brand, a former general counsel for the House of Representatives. “I don’t know if the Congress knows.”

Nonetheless, Democrats are eager to highlight what they view as abuses of power, including a succession of investigations the department has launched into the president’s perceived adversaries, many of which have been rejected by grand juries, dismissed by judges or have otherwise stalled without apparent progress.

In just the eventful weeks leading up to the election, the department unsuccessfully sought an indictment against former White House aide Cassidy Hutchinson, accelerated an investigation into Democratic Rep. Ilhan Omar, employed an unusual maneuver to file a fresh criminal case against former FBI Director James Comey and charged two ex-FBI officials in a complaint that was swiftly dismissed by a judge.
Political pressure from the White House is unlikely to wane given the promotion of Stephen Miller, a devoted Trump loyalist, to chief of staff.

And Justice Department leadership has suggested it won’t let Democrats’ threats of investigations deter its pursuit of the White House’s priorities, and may become even more aggressive in pressing the president’s causes.

“We will not back down. This will not slow us down. This will not stop us,” Blanche said in a Fox News interview Monday. “President Trump has two years remaining in this administration and you better believe that we’re going to use it effectively.”

In a call with U.S. attorneys across the country this week, a top Blanche aide, Aakash Singh, told prosecutors to prepare to be on “wartime” footing, and suggested more U.S. attorneys may be pushed out after a spate of postelection departures, according to people familiar with the call who spoke on the condition of anonymity to discuss internal department discussions.

The Justice Department said the “‘wartime’ reference had everything to do with public safety,” noting that some “newly elected state and local leaders are no longer interested in partnering with federal law enforcement.”

Any additional U.S. attorney departures would be on top of a string of significant departures in the days after the election, when the Senate-confirmed leaders of the department’s National Security, Civil and Civil Rights divisions all announced their resignations. The divisions will have temporary leaders but are unlikely to get Senate-confirmed ones in light of the Democratic majority.

“What that means for DOJ, potentially, is just a lot of inaction, with tough decisions not being made because typically those tough decisions are made by confirmed people at the top of the components,” said Greg Brower, a former U.S. attorney in Nevada during President George W. Bush’s administration who was later the FBI’s chief congressional affairs official.
body_zh: 司法部作为白宫的延伸部分运行了近两年，不受共和党控制的国会的限制
埃里克·塔克 (ERIC TUCKER) 美联社和阿兰娜·德金·里彻 (ALANNA DURKIN RICHER) 美联社报道
华盛顿——近两年来，司法部一直充当白宫的延伸，不受共和党控制的国会的限制，对唐纳德·特朗普总统的敌人进行调查，解雇了一批职业雇员，并为全国各地法官一再认为法律上可疑的政府立场辩护。
现在，民主党在国会的全面胜利已经改变了华盛顿的权力平衡，引发了对这些行动和其他行动的一系列预期调查，以及现任司法部迄今为止一直设法避开的多数党的审查。
至少在公开场合，该部门似乎并没有因环境的改变而屈服。
司法部长托德·布兰奇表示，该部门将与国会合作，但也坚称“我们不会在共和党总统的议程上退缩”。与此同时，一名高级助手在电话中告诉检察官准备进入“战时”状态，一名美国检察官公开警告一名民主党高级官员有关计划中的国会调查。
这为一场拳击运动奠定了基础，因为民主党人承诺加入本已持怀疑态度的法院来遏制特朗普政府，而司法部因数千名职业雇员的流失和高级领导人的离职而精疲力尽，承诺推进其议程。
尽管民主党握有木槌，但他们缺乏保证共和党合作的万无一失的方法。诉讼可能需要数年时间，传票可能很难执行，因不遵守规定而提出的藐视法庭刑事案件将被送往特朗普政府司法部，而司法部几乎肯定不会采取行动。
“这是一场僵局，我还不知道答案是什么，”众议院前总法律顾问斯坦·布兰德说。 “我不知道国会是否知道。”
尽管如此，民主党人仍急于强调他们认为的滥用权力行为，包括该部门对总统的所谓对手发起的一系列调查，其中许多调查被大陪审团拒绝，被法官驳回，或者因其他原因而停滞不前，没有明显进展。
在大选前的动荡几周内，该部门未能成功起诉前白宫助手卡西迪·哈钦森，加快了对民主党众议员伊尔汗·奥马尔的调查，采取了不寻常的策略对前联邦调查局局长詹姆斯·科米提起新的刑事案件，并在一项指控中指控了两名前联邦调查局官员，但该指控很快被法官驳回。
鉴于特朗普的忠实拥护者史蒂芬·米勒(Stephen Miller)晋升为幕僚长，来自白宫的政治压力不太可能减弱。
司法部领导层表示，不会让民主党的调查威胁阻止其对白宫优先事项的追求，并且可能会更加积极地推动总统的事业。
“我们不会退缩。这不会让我们放慢脚步。这不会阻止我们，”布兰奇周一在接受福克斯新闻采访时表示。 “特朗普总统在本届政府的任期还剩两年，你最好相信我们会有效地利用它。”
据知情人士透露，在本周与全国各地美国检察官的电话会议中，布兰奇的高级助手阿卡什·辛格告诉检察官，要做好“战时”准备，并建议更多的美国检察官在选举后一连串离职后可能会被解雇。
司法部表示，“‘战时’的提法与公共安全密切相关”，并指出一些“新当选的州和地方领导人不再有兴趣与联邦执法部门合作”。
任何额外的美国检察官离职都将是选举后几天内一系列重大离职事件的基础上，参议院确认的该部门国家安全、民权和民权部门的领导人均宣布辞职。这些部门将有临时领导人，但鉴于民主党占多数，不太可能获得参议院确认的领导人。
“这对司法部来说可能意味着大量无所作为，无法做出艰难的决定，因为这些艰难的决定通常是由已确认的高层人士做出的，”乔治·W·布什总统执政期间内华达州前联邦检察官、后来担任联邦调查局首席国会事务官员的格雷格·布劳尔说。

title_en: New congressman faces sexual harassment allegation
title_zh: 新任国会议员面临性骚扰指控
summary: House Democrats are investigating an allegation of sexual harassment against Brian Poindexter, who defeated embattled GOP Rep. Max Miller.
summary_zh: 众议院民主党人正在调查针对布莱恩·波因德克斯特的性骚扰指控，他击败了陷入困境的共和党众议员马克斯·米勒。
body_en: Democrats investigating sexual harassment allegation against newly elected congressman Brian Poindexter - CBS News
Washington — House Democrats are investigating an allegation of sexual harassment against Brian Poindexter, who defeated embattled GOP Rep. Max Miller of Ohio in last week's elections.

The Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee, House Democrats' campaign arm, said Friday that it had hired an independent firm to investigate "any instance of inappropriate behavior, conduct interviews and gather the facts."
"The DCCC has been made aware of the allegations and takes them seriously," the group's executive director, Julie Merz, said in a statement.
A spokesperson for Poindexter's campaign characterized his actions as "an innocuous compliment to a volunteer."

"He heard later that it made her feel uncomfortable and he felt awful," the spokesperson said in a statement. "When Brian learned about this, we immediately began to work to get to the bottom of it with an outside HR firm. Neither Brian nor the campaign ever wants anyone to feel uncomfortable."
The investigation comes as Congress grapples with how to overhaul how it handles allegations of sexual misconduct as numerous lawmakers have faced complaints.

The DCCC was made aware of the allegations from two political action committees — the Blue Dog PAC and the Congressional Progressive Caucus PAC — which said they were informed of a report of alleged sexual harassment in the final days before the election.

"We informed the DCCC and connected the individual with legal advocacy and support services so she could determine how she wanted to proceed," the PACs said in a joint statement Friday. "The individual requested that we did not disclose any details about this publicly because she did not want her identity becoming public and she wanted an opportunity to determine how she wanted to proceed while protecting herself."
The PACs said they pulled their endorsements from Poindexter "pending the investigation being completed."

title_en: Tanker collides with cruise ship on Mississippi River in New Orleans
title_zh: 新奥尔良密西西比河上油轮与游轮相撞
summary: Large emergency response under way to rescue people from the water, with overnight cruise ship on its side New Orleans river collision – latest updates A tanker collided with a river cruise ship docked on the Mississippi River in New Orleans on Friday afternoo
summary_zh: 大型紧急响应正在进行中，从水中营救人员，夜间游轮在新奥尔良河一侧发生碰撞 - 最新更新
body_en: ‘Miracle on the Mississippi’: all accounted for after tanker collides with cruise ship in New Orleans
No passengers or crew members were killed or critically hurt after the crash on the Mississippi River, officials say

In what the city’s mayor declared a “miracle on the Mississippi”, all passengers were accounted for – with none killed or critically hurt – after a tanker collided with a river cruise ship docked on the Mississippi River in New Orleans on Friday afternoon.

Thirty-two people were taken to local hospitals after the Atlantic Asphalt tanker struck American Cruise Lines’s American Heritage at about 12.30pm – but none of their injuries were considered critical, New Orleans’s mayor, Helena Moreno, said at a news conference.

Zero passengers or crew members were unaccounted for, Moreno said. She attributed that fact to a hectic but effective multi-agency rescue effort after the American Heritage was struck and a number of people ended up in the river, whose waters are cold and its currents are infamously perilous.
That “truly is a miracle on the Mississippi,” Moreno said near the scene of the crash, as a group of fellow officials around her applauded.
The American Heritage had about 129 passengers – in addition to crew members – onboard when it was hit, Port of New Orleans press secretary Kimberly Curth said in a statement.
About two hours before that, the American Heritage had docked at the port to begin passenger disembarkation, Curth said.

Officials did not immediately provide details about what caused the crash. Moreno said investigators would explore whether there was some loss of steering on the Atlantic Asphalt before it struck the American Heritage, as an emergency response source had said earlier – but that had not been immediately confirmed.

The website marinetraffic.com showed the Atlantic Asphalt’s path was seemingly uneventful as it went around the Mississippi River bend near New Orleans’ Algiers Point neighborhood. It had just made it past the Crescent City Connection bridge linking New Orleans’ central business district and the community’s Algiers section when it began heading generally to its starboard – or right – side.

Video provided to Guardian reporting partner WWL Louisiana showed the Atlantic Asphalt then T-boned the side of the American Heritage. The cruise ship eventually slowly rolled on to its side where it was struck, according to the video, which the CBS affiliate obtained from Barry Kern, proprietor of Mardi Gras World, a tourist attraction near the scene of the crash.
One witness, Jamie Holford, told local NBC News affiliate WDSU that it took 15 minutes “from impact to where it rolled over”.
“Surreal,” Holford said. “That’s what that was.”

Maritime law expert Martin J Davies of New Orleans’ Tulane University told local Fox affiliate WVUE that the Atlantic Asphalt was fortunate to have not hit the Crescent City Connection, which is estimated to carry about 160,000 cars daily.
“This is obviously a really bad incident,” Davies said. “But it could also have struck the bridge, which it didn’t.”

A video from WDSU showed crew members of a tugboat working to pull people in lifejackets or holding on to flotation rings out of the river. An emergency response that drew in firefighters, US Coast Guard helicopter and boat crews, as well as port and city police – among others – also helped pull out people who ended up in the water in plain view of cameras and eyewitnesses.

Video from WVUE showed the American Heritage slowly rolling on to its side with the Atlantic Asphalt nearby a s first responders ran briskly in the foreground to help. One image on social media showed people climbing on the side of the cruise boat – specifically, on stateroom balconies – after it was struck, with chairs and tables strewn about.

An employee at the Ernest N Morial Convention Center next to the scene of Friday’s crash said she realized something was awry when she could see from her vantage point that the tip of the American Heritage was tilted. She then grasped the nature of situation when she heard desperate shrieks.

“People were screaming for help,” said the employee, who asked to not be named. She recalled how she and colleagues assembled wheelchairs, water and other items in case survivors would soon need them.
The American Heritage’s passengers were brought inside the New Orleans port’s administration building, next to the convention center.
body_zh: “密西西比河上的奇迹”：油轮在新奥尔良与游轮相撞后全部遇难
官员称，密西西比河坠机事件后，没有乘客或机组人员死亡或重伤
周五下午，一艘油轮与一艘停靠在新奥尔良密西西比河上的内河游轮相撞，该市市长宣称这是“密西西比河上的奇迹”，所有乘客均已安全抵达，没有人死亡或重伤。
新奥尔良市市长海伦娜·莫雷诺 (Helena Moreno) 在新闻发布会上表示，大西洋沥青油轮于中午 12 点 30 分左右撞上美国邮轮公司的 American Heritage 邮轮，造成 32 人被送往当地医院，但没有人受伤。
莫雷诺说，零名乘客或机组人员下落不明。她将这一事实归因于美国遗产遭到袭击后，许多人落入河中，该河的水很冷，水流也非常危险，因此多机构展开了紧张而有效的救援工作。
莫雷诺在事故现场附近说道，“这确实是密西西比河上的一个奇迹”，周围的一群官员为她鼓掌。
新奥尔良港新闻秘书金伯利·柯斯 (Kimberly Curth) 在一份声明中表示，美国遗产号被击中时，除了船员外，船上还有大约 129 名乘客。
柯斯说，大约在此之前两个小时，美国遗产号已停靠在港口，开始乘客下船。
官员们没有立即提供坠机原因的详细信息。莫雷诺表示，正如应急响应消息人士早些时候所说，调查人员将调查“大西洋沥青”号在撞上“美国遗产号”之前是否存在转向损失，但这一点尚未得到立即证实。
Marinetraffic.com 网站显示，Atlantic Asphalt 的道路看似平安无事，它绕过新奥尔良阿尔及尔角附近的密西西比河弯道。它刚刚通过连接新奥尔良中央商务区和社区阿尔及尔部分的新月城连接桥，就开始向右舷或右侧行驶。
提供给《卫报》报道合作伙伴 WWL 路易斯安那州的视频显示，大西洋沥青随后在美国遗产号的一侧形成了丁字形。哥伦比亚广播公司附属机构从事故现场附近的狂欢节世界的老板巴里·科恩那里获得的视频显示，这艘游轮最终慢慢地滚到了被撞的一侧。
一位目击者杰米·霍尔福德 (Jamie Holford) 告诉当地 NBC 新闻附属机构 WDSU，“从撞击到翻滚”花了 15 分钟。
“超现实，”霍尔福德说。 “就是这样。”
新奥尔良杜兰大学的海事法专家马丁·J·戴维斯 (Martin J Davies) 告诉福克斯当地附属机构 WVUE，Atlantic Asphalt 很幸运没有撞到 Crescent City Connection，估计每天运载约 160,000 辆汽车。
“这显然是一起非常糟糕的事件，”戴维斯说。 “但它也可能撞到了桥，但它没有。”
WDSU 的一段视频显示，一艘拖船的船员正在努力将穿着救生衣的人员或抓住浮环从河中拉出。消防队员、美国海岸警卫队直升机和船员以及港口和城市警察等的紧急响应也帮助在摄像机和目击者的清晰视野下救出了落水的人。
来自 WVUE 的视频显示，美国遗产号慢慢地向一侧滚动，附近有大西洋沥青，第一批救援人员迅速跑到前景提供帮助。社交媒体上的一张图片显示，游轮被撞后，人们爬上游轮的一侧，特别是在客舱阳台上，椅子和桌子散落一地。
周五事故现场附近的欧内斯特·莫里尔会议中心的一名员工表示，当她从自己的有利位置看到美国遗产号的尖端倾斜时，她意识到有些不对劲。当她听到绝望的尖叫声时，她明白了情况的本质。
“人们尖叫着寻求帮助，”这位不愿透露姓名的员工说。她回忆起她和同事如何组装轮椅、水和其他物品，以防幸存者很快需要它们。
美国遗产号的乘客被带到会议中心旁边的新奥尔良港口行政大楼内。

Kai Wright of the Guardian podcast Stateside will speak with author and environmentalist Bill McKibben – and we’d like to hear your questions
Was the climate crisis one of your top political priorities during the midterm elections? We want to hear from you: what do you want political leaders to do about it in 2027?

Democrats will control the House and Senate in the new year, and they have a long list of priorities ahead of them. But it remains to be seen just how much they will focus on one of the most pressing issues of our times: the climate crisis. The UN declared this summer that, despite some progress, it is now “unavoidable” that the globe will heat past the point that scientists say will threaten human health. Despite these terrifying predictions, the US remains absent from global efforts to limit the impacts of the climate crisis.

Environmentalist and Guardian columnist Bill McKibben has been ringing the alarm for decades. But in his most recent book, Here Comes the Sun , he’s argued that we’re at a unique moment of opportunity. The science and the markets have given us the tools to solve the crisis – we just need the politics to catch up. So what does he think is politically possible now? And what would you like to ask McKibben about this moment of peril and opportunity?
